sam.sales: Heads-up — customer on the POC can intermittently resolve our private model endpoint to a public IP. Their app sometimes gets TLS handshake timeouts. Blocker for closing this week. Can we swarm?
eng.anna: :eyes: Ok can you paste the dig/nslookup from one of their failing hosts and any curl/tls logs?
customer_sre: Copying outputs from customer box (Linux). They said it flips between IPs.
customer_sre: ```bash
$ dig +short model.private.redwood.internal
10.2.5.12
54.211.22.33
$ curl -v https://model.private.redwood.internal --max-time 10
* Connected to 54.211.22.33 (54.211.22.33) port 443(#0)
* TLS handshake timeout
```
kevin.ops: That 54.211.22.33 is one of our public LB IPs. Looks like split DNS or a recursive cache returning stale answer. Do they have an on-prem DNS caching appliance?
maria.k: They mentioned a caching proxy (BlueCache) in their corporate network that sits in front of their DNS. TTLs could be being ignored. Ask them to flush caches or test with 8.8.8.8 directly.
eng.anna: Also check VPC outbound NAT/egress rules — if their VNet NATs to a public IP and then hairpins back through our public LB, TLS SNI/mTLS could fail. Request traceroute too.
customer_sre: Traceroute shows hop 6 goes to their firewall then to internet, then back to our public LB. They do have an egress NAT.
kevin.ops: That confirms hairpinning. Two mitigation paths: 1) use VPC PrivateLink / interface endpoint so traffic never leaves their VNet, or 2) fix split-horizon so private host resolves to the private IP only. For short-term we can provide a private endpoint token for their account and a one-off route suggestion.
sam.sales: The customer wants an ETA. If PrivateLink is needed, how long to enable for a POC? Any cost implications?
maria.k: For a POC we can spin up an interface endpoint in their region in ~2 business days if they give VPC details and allow us to create the endpoint. We'll document expected egress costs — mostly standard data processing + endpoint hour. I can draft pricing line items.
eng.anna: Short-term troubleshooting: ask them to add an /etc/hosts entry pointing model.private.redwood.internal -> 10.2.5.12 and retest. That rules out cache. Also try `dig @<their-dns> model.private.redwood.internal +trace` to see where the public IP is coming from.
customer_sre: Tried hosts file mapping -> curl succeeds to 10.2.5.12 and TLS is fine. So it's definitely DNS resolution.
infra_bot: ALERT: TLS_HANDSHAKE_FAIL count increased by 57 in last 30m for customer: acct-7923. (link to alert)
sam.sales: Great repro. Next steps: 1) Maria to send PrivateLink instructions and pricing, 2) Customer to flush on-prem DNS cache or add split-horizon record, 3) Eng Anna to prepare diagnostic snippet and a temporary hosts-based workaround for POC.
maria.k: I'll prepare the PrivateLink steps + a one-off quote by EOD. :thumbsup:
eng.anna: I'll share a diagnostics checklist and a curl + openssl s_client snippet they can run.
kevin.ops: If they can't get PrivateLink approved, we can also offer Dedicated capacity in their VNet (longer lead). I'll note the ops playbook.
sam.sales: Thanks all — tagging @customer_sre please confirm when they flush cache or if they want us to set up the temporary endpoint.
customer_sre: Will confirm with infra team and loop back in 2 hours. Thanks everyone. :pray:
